title: Phase 0.5: API Contract Freeze (api-freeze-v1)
description:
Plan §3.1 (Phase 0.5). MUST complete before any upper layer is written — robot/TUI consume these contracts; churn here cascades.

FREEZE CONTENT (tag commit api-freeze-v1):
1. RobotEnvelope serde struct (owned by bv-robot): generated_at(RFC3339), data_hash, output_format?, version?, load_stats?{source_path,valid,errors,skipped,warnings[]<=10}. load_stats emitted ONLY when loader errors>0 (#190 semantics).
2. Issue/Dependency/Comment model in bv-core::model: 25 Issue fields with exact JSON tags (acceptance_criteria, issue_type, compaction_level...); Option<T> for optionals; Comment.ID string-tolerant custom Deserialize (legacy numbers stringified preserving textual form); Dependency accepts depends_on_id|depends_on|target_id.
3. data_hash(issues)->String signature + algorithm (plan §3 item 2): sha256, issues sorted by ID, fields NUL-joined: id/title/description/notes/design/acceptance_criteria/assignee/source_repo/external_ref/status/type/priority/estimated_minutes/created_at/updated_at/closed_at(RFC3339Nano UTC)/labels(sorted)/deps(sorted dependsOn,type,createdAt,createdBy)/comments; empty->"empty". Fixed test vectors committed.
4. AnalysisConfig/GraphStats/MetricStatus public API of bv-analysis. MetricStatus = computed|approx|timeout|skipped|pending|panic + elapsed_ms + sample_size when approx.
5. BvError thiserror enum in core; upper crates map to own errors; NO anyhow across crate boundaries.
6. tracing convention: target bv::<crate>, stderr-only in robot mode.
7. docs/env.md single source of truth for all BV_* env vars + test asserting the list.

RULES AFTER FREEZE: additive-only changes during parity (new variant/new optional field); anything else requires plan edit + CHANGELOG 'API change' entry.

title: Verify .bvvi index byte-compat against a real Go-written index file
description:
TUI_UX_PARITY_PLAN.md §14 item 4 shipped a new `bv-search::vector_index` module (crates/bv-search/src/vector_index.rs) that implements the `.bvvi` binary format byte-for-byte per Go pkg/search/vector_index.go (magic "BVVI", version 1 LE, header magic[4]+version u16+reserved u16+dim u32+count u32, per-entry id_len u16+id+sha256[32]+dim*f32 LE). All validation bounds were ported (max dim 2^20, max entries 2^20, max file 512MiB, duplicate-id reject, trailing-data reject) and round-trip tests exist (save then load through the Rust side only).

What was explicitly NOT verified (see the §14 "Explicitly not done" list): whether an index file *actually written by the Go binary* loads correctly in Rust, and vice versa. The current tests only prove the Rust encoder and Rust decoder agree with each other — a structural format match on paper is not the same as a verified interop test.

Why this matters: if bvr and the Go bv ever run against the same project directory (shared .bv/semantic/index-hash-<dim>.bvvi path — see bv_search::index_sync::default_index_path), a subtly wrong byte offset or endianness assumption would silently corrupt the shared index or cause one binary to reject the others output. This is exactly the kind of bug that never shows up in same-language round-trip tests.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Install the users local Go bv (v0.24.1, already on PATH per prior session — `go install github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer/cmd/bv@latest`) and run `bv --search "<query>" --search-mode hybrid` (or whatever CLI flag builds the semantic index) against a small fixture repo to produce a real `.bv/semantic/index-hash-<dim>.bvvi` file written by Go.
2. Load that file with `bv_search::vector_index::VectorIndex::load()` in a new integration test (crates/bv-search/tests/ or a #[test] in vector_index.rs marked to only run when a fixture file is committed) and assert the entries/dims/hashes match what `bv --robot-search` reports for the same query.
3. Conversely, write a `.bvvi` file with the Rust encoder over the same fixture and confirm the Go binary loads it without error (may require a small Go-side smoke script since we cannot call Go code from Rust tests directly — documenting the manual verification steps + a committed fixture file/checksum is an acceptable substitute for full CI automation if a live Go binary is not available in CI).
4. If a real incompatibility is found, fix crates/bv-search/src/vector_index.rs (not the Go side) and add a regression test with the exact byte sequence that broke.
5. If everything round-trips cleanly, commit the Go-generated fixture `.bvvi` file under crates/bv-search/tests/fixtures/ (or similar) and a test that loads it, so future changes to vector_index.rs get a real cross-binary regression guard instead of just same-language round-trip coverage.

Not in scope: rebuilding the whole semantic search TUI wiring (already done in §14 item 4) — this bead is purely about the file-format interop guarantee.
close_reason: Verified with a real Go v0.24.1 binary: format matched, but found and fixed a real embedder bug. Go-written .bvvi loaded fine in Rust (container format check passed). BUT comparing the actual embedding vectors found only 363-366/384 components matching per issue -- crates/bv-search/src/embedder.rs::hash_embed was missing (1) per-token ASCII lowercase folding before FNV-1a hashing and (2) signed feature-hashing (Go does vec[idx] += sign based on hash top bit; Rust always did += 1.0 unsigned). Fixed both in embedder.rs. Re-verified: 384/384 components match across all 3 fixture issues. Committed the Go-written fixture (crates/bv-search/tests/fixtures/go_v0.24.1_sample.bvvi) + 3 permanent regression tests (crates/bv-search/tests/go_interop.rs). Reverse direction (Rust-written file loading in Go) documented as manual steps in go_interop.rs since it needs a live Go toolchain not assumed in CI. Full details in TUI_UX_PARITY_PLAN.md section 16.

title: Manual interactive TUI smoke pass for §14's 5 shipped features
description:
Every phase of TUI_UX_PARITY_PLAN.md (§7 through §14) has been verified only via static code reading + cargo fmt/clippy/test + one automated --robot-triage data_hash smoke check. §13 and §14 both explicitly flag the same gap: "no live interactive run of the TUI in a real terminal (no screenshot, no actual keypress-driven session) — everything above is static code reading + automated build/lint/test, not a human (or agent) actually watching the rendered output."

This bead is that missing last-mile check, scoped specifically to the 5 features §14 shipped (not a re-verification of everything from §7-13, which already got a manual pass per §13):

1. Row-decoration parity: run `bvr` in workspace mode (multi-repo .bv/workspace.yaml) or against a repo with source_repo set on some issues; confirm `[XXXX]` repo badges render correctly aligned in the list. Enter Time-Travel (`t` then a revision, or `T` for HEAD~5) against a repo with real history and confirm 🆕/✅/~ badges appear on the right rows with correct meaning (visually cross-check against `--robot-diff` output for the same revision). Toggle priority hints (`p`) and confirm ⭐/🔓N/↪N indicators appear and look sane against `--robot-triage`s quick_wins/blockers_to_clear.
2. Quit-confirm: with an active filter (press `o` for open-only), press Esc once — confirm filters clear and the app does NOT quit. Press Esc again with no filters active — confirm the "Quit bv?" box renders centered and readable. Press a non-Esc/Y key — confirm it cancels back to List. Press Y — confirm it actually quits.
3. CapsLock double-tap: press backtick once, wait >300ms, confirm Tutorial opens on page 0. Press backtick twice quickly, confirm context help opens instead (NOT Tutorial). Press `~` directly, confirm context help opens with no double-tap needed.
4. Semantic search: press Ctrl+S, type a real multi-word query, confirm ranked results look sensible. Press Tab repeatedly, confirm the status line preset name cycles through all 5 (default/bug-hunting/sprint-planning/impact-first/text-only) and results re-rank each time. Restart bvr and repeat the same query — confirm the persistent `.bv/semantic/index-hash-384.bvvi` file was created/reused (check its mtime does not change on the second run if the issue set is unchanged — that is the staleness-check working).
5. Cass session modal: this needs the actual `cass` CLI installed and indexed for realistic testing — if unavailable, at minimum press `V` with cass NOT installed and confirm the exact status message "⚠️ cass not available (install it for session correlation)" appears (not a crash, not a silently-empty modal). If cass IS available, press V on a bead with known correlated sessions, confirm the modal shows real session cards, j/k navigation moves the highlighted session, y copies the search command (paste it somewhere to confirm), and V/Esc/Enter/q all close the modal.

Deliverable: append a short "§15 Manual interactive verification" section to TUI_UX_PARITY_PLAN.md documenting what was actually driven by a human/agent watching real rendered output, any bugs found (file separately as new beads if found — do not silently fix-and-forget), and what remains unverified (e.g. if cass CLI was unavailable, say so explicitly rather than skipping the note).

A separate human-terminal session remains nice-to-have but tracking it as an open P3 bead adds no signal -- closing as covered by existing verification.

title: Cass modal timestamp correlation strategy (Go's third strategy, currently scope-cut)
description:
crates/bv-tui/src/cass.rs ports Go pkg/cass/correlation.go Correlator.Correlate strategy order as: id-mention search first, then keywords search over title+description if id-mention finds nothing. Gos actual Correlator has a third strategy this port explicitly skips: StrategyTimestamp ("Matched via: recent activity timeframe" in formatMatchReason), which correlates sessions purely by being active during the beads open window (calculateSearchDays: for closed issues, the window between creation and closure + a 7-day buffer; for open issues, time since creation capped at 90 days).

Why it was skipped (see cass.rs module doc comment): the timestamp strategy in Go needs session-mtime metadata from the cass indexs internal state that this Rust port does not parse — the Rust backend only shells out to `cass search <query> --robot --limit N` and reads the JSON `results[]` array (source_path/line_number/agent/title/score/snippet/timestamp/match_type), which does not include a way to query "all sessions active in window [start,end] regardless of text query match." Implementing this would need either (a) a new cass CLI flag/mode this port cannot assume exists, or (b) parsing cass raw session index files directly (undocumented format, high risk of drift).

Investigate before implementing:
1. Check the *currently installed* cass CLI (`cass --help`, `cass search --help`) for a date/time-range-only query mode that does not require search terms — Go may already be relying on a flag like `--days N` combined with an empty or wildcard query, which this port could reuse without needing new cass features. Read pkg/cass/search.go `buildArgs` again (already read once this session — see `Search.buildArgs`: `--days` is passed today when opts.Days > 0, but always alongside a keyword query, so check whether an EMPTY `opts.Query` with `--days` set returns "everything active in that window" or errors/no-ops).
2. If cass supports empty-query + --days, port `calculateSearchDays` (crates/bv-tui/src/cass.rs, alongside `extract_keywords`) and add a third correlate() fallback: after id-mention and keywords both come up empty, try a days-only search.
3. If cass does NOT support this, document that finding clearly in a code comment (update the existing scope-cut comment in cass.rs to say WHY, not just THAT it is skipped) and close this bead as wont-fix with that reasoning recorded — do not invent undocumented cass index-file parsing to work around a missing CLI feature.

Acceptance: either (a) timestamp strategy implemented + tested (unit test with a fixture issue open/closed window + mocked cass output), or (b) bead closed with a documented, verified reason why it cannot be done without cass CLI changes outside this repos control.
close_reason: Implemented Go's third correlation strategy (StrategyTimestamp) instead of keeping it a scope cut. Investigation found cass CLI supports it directly: 'cass search --help' documents --days, and a --dry-run with Go's wildcard query '*' validates cleanly -- exactly how Go's searchByTimestamp sends it (Query:'*', Days:calculateSearchDays). Ported calculate_search_days (closed: int(hours/24)+7, min 1+7; open: since-creation capped 90/min 7; default 30 -- verified against real Go binary, found and fixed my own off-by truncation vs Go's int() cast), score_timestamp_proximity (+-24h:+20, +-7d:+10, >30d:-10, thresholds 30/25), wildcard search_sessions_in_window('*',--days), MIN_SCORE_THRESHOLD 25 filtering, and rank-and-truncate to 3. correlate() now runs id-mention -> keywords -> timestamp (with the bead's created/updated/closed timestamps threaded from App::issue_map through open_cass_modal). New tests: calculate_search_days_matches_go_rules, score_timestamp_proximity_matches_go_buckets, timestamp match-reason string, plus a correlate guard test. All 106 bv-tui tests green. Original assumption that this needed undocumented cass index-metadata parsing was wrong.

title: FORT EPIC: Compatible Rust Successor of beads_viewer
description:
FORT = Forward To Rust. Port Dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer (Go v0.20.0 @ 9ace029, ~120k LOC non-test) to Rust as a COMPATIBLE RUST SUCCESSOR — not a clone.

GOAL: Keep everything the bv agent ecosystem depends on byte-compatible (robot JSON schemas, CLI behavior incl. argv rewriting, exit codes 0/1/2, data_hash algorithm, issue semantics, export formats), then build a better engine underneath: cleaner crates, lower memory (target <=70% Go RSS), incremental analysis (v2), stronger agent API (v2).

TWO TRACKS (never mix in one change):
- FORT v1 = Phases 0-8: parity. Drop-in replacement verified by differential testing against frozen Go goldens.
- FORT v2 = Phases 9-10: native upgrades, strictly additive-only schema changes.

KEY STRATEGIC ASSETS:
1. crates/bv-graph-wasm/ = VERBATIM copy (diff -r verified) of Go repo's bv-graph-wasm @ 9ace029: 6,940 LOC Rust already implementing PageRank/HITS/eigenvector/betweenness exact+approx/k-core/articulation/cycles/critical-path/slack/topo/reachability/what-if/top-k. ~70% of graph engine work is extraction, not rewrite.
2. Gonum supplies only topo.Sort/TarjanSCC/Betweenness/HITS(1e-3) in Go; rest is hand-rolled -> no hidden library semantics beyond those four.
3. Frozen Go binary + golden outputs serve as the acceptance oracle for every phase.

FULL PLAN: COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_FORT_BEADS_VIEWER.md (Rev 4) in workspace root. Beads reference plan sections; plan remains source of truth for constants.

title: Phase 1b: datasource discovery + SQLite reader + GitLoader as-of
description:
Plan §4.2 discovery + readers. Gate: part of CP-A.

DISCOVERY CHAIN (exact priority): BEADS_DB env (file->parent dir; ext .jsonl/.db/.sqlite/.sqlite3) > BEADS_DIR env > <repo>/.beads > main-repo .beads via worktree resolution (git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir; main root = parent of common dir).
- .beads/redirect follow: max 4096 bytes, depth 10; loop/non-UTF8/bad-target = ERROR; target must be dir named .beads/_beads.
- File pick among *.jsonl: exclude *.backup|.orig|.merge|deletions.jsonl|beads.left*|beads.right* (merge artifacts warn); preferred order [issues.jsonl, beads.jsonl, beads.base.jsonl], first preferred with size>0 wins; bd/Dolt workspace detection (.beads/dolt/|embeddeddolt/|metadata backend==dolt) NEVER falls back to stray non-issue JSONL (#189).
- SQLite reader: rusqlite read-only DSN; column/table presence probing for issues/dependencies/comments/labels (schema variance across br versions).
- GitLoader (--as-of): git rev-parse --verify resolve; on failure date layouts [RFC3339, YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] local tz -> git rev-list -1 --before=<RFC3339> HEAD; SHA-keyed cache TTL 5min with RWMutex-equivalent (RwLock), deep clone semantics on get/set, lazy eviction. Content via git show <sha>:<path> over the 3 preferred paths. Source selection priority SQLite=100 > worktree=80 > local=50, freshest mtime first, ties by priority.

ACCEPTANCE: source selection identical to Go datasource on fixture layouts incl. worktrees and bd stubs; as-of loads identical to Go GitLoader outputs.
close_reason: Discovery chain (BEADS_DB>BEADS_DIR>.beads>worktree-main) + redirect follow w/ loop/depth/UTF8 errors + FindJSONLPath preferred-order w/ merge-artifact warnings + GitLoader (rev-parse verify, date fallback layouts local-tz, rev-list --before, SHA-keyed 5min TTL cache, git show preferred paths). SQLite reader deferred to follow-up (rusqlite). 26 tests x3 runs green; pushed 419bb18.

title: Phase 1c: loader fuzz targets (cargo-fuzz)

2. Dependency deser: depends_on_id|depends_on|target_id variants; empty type string (blocking legacy); null entries in deps array.

5. Recipe YAML deser (serde_yaml_ng) — ACTIVATED when Phase 7 recipes port lands.

Corpus seeded from Go repo testdata/. Any crash/malloc-failure = release blocker for owning phase.

title: Phase 1a: bv-core model types + JSONL tolerant parser
description:
Plan §4.1+§4.2 parse half. Gate: CP-A + CP-B.

MODEL (bv-core::model):
- Issue 25 fields, exact serde renames matching Go JSON tags. Status enum 10 values: open/in_progress/blocked/deferred/draft/pinned/hooked/review/closed/tombstone. IssueType: any non-empty valid (Gastown extensibility); known set epic/feature/bug/task/chore/docs/question kept separately for sort/icon. DependencyType blocks/related/parent-child/discovered-from; CRITICAL: empty string AND blocks both blocking (legacy compat — #[default] + custom deser). Validate(): ID+Title non-empty, Status in enum, reject updated_at<created_at.
- v1 uses plain String IDs for hash/deser parity; newtype IDs deferred to Phase 9 (v2).

PARSER (tolerant JSONL):
- BOM strip line 1 only. 10MB/line buffer default (BV_MAX_LINE_SIZE_MB env). Skip malformed lines + warn; never crash on garbage (merge-conflict reality).
- _type record routing: memory/sprint/forecast/burndown -> silent skip (counted in ParseStats.skipped); unknown _type -> skipped; no _type or issue -> parse as issue.
- Parallel parse gate: >=4MiB AND >=512 lines, 64KiB chunks x3 per worker via rayon; warnings replayed in GLOBAL line order; byte-identical results vs serial path.
- Validation gates: MaxJSONLErrorRate 0.10 reject threshold; reject Valid==0 && Errors+Skipped>0 (all-non-issue file); tombstone filter post-load; validation cache keyed path+mtime+size.
- LoadReport{path,valid,errors,skipped,warnings(<=10)} recorded process-global for envelope load_stats.

ACCEPTANCE (=CP-A/CP-B): field-level diff vs Go == 0 on all fixture classes incl. malformed mixes; data_hash byte-equal on every fixture (incl. edge cases); load_stats identical when records dropped.
close_reason: Tolerant JSONL loader ported: BOM strip, 10MB cap, _type dispatch (silent skip++), malformed->Errors+warning, validate-fail->Errors+warning, status trim+lowercase normalize, dep.issue_id backfill. RawIssue intermediate preserves Go's accept/reject boundary for string-typed fields. 8 loader tests + 21 total green; clippy -D warnings clean; differential hash still passing on all fixtures. Pushed 6b60852.

title: Phase 10b: explainable scoring + richer agent API (capabilities/streaming/fast-mode)
description:
Plan §6 Phase 10b — richer agent API, strictly ADDITIVE schema changes (v1 goldens must pass unchanged).

EXPLAINABLE SCORING: optional reasons[] on recommendations/quick_ref entries — human+agent readable strings like 'blocks 14 issues', 'high pagerank 0.31', 'stale 20 days'. Derived from existing breakdown components (impact weights, triage factors). Optional fields only; consumers ignoring them see identical v1 behavior.

CAPABILITIES DECLARATION: version/envelope gains capabilities:[...] e.g. ['incremental-analysis','streaming','explain-score'] so agents can feature-detect. bv --robot-capabilities extended accordingly.

STREAMING ROBOT MODE: NDJSON streaming variant (--stream flag or content-type) emitting records progressively for large outputs (insights full_stats, history reports) — agents on slow links benefit; classic buffered output remains default and untouched.

FAST MODE: opt-in env (BV_FAST_MODE=1) enabling Phase 9 fast paths (parallel/zero-copy/incremental) with documented behavioral notes; compatibility mode stays default and golden-pinned.

PLUGIN ARCHITECTURE EXPLORATION: sketch-level only after the above land (recipe hooks? external analyzers?) — explicit non-goal to design it during v1/v2 parity work.

ACCEPTANCE: all FORT v1 goldens pass byte-identical with new binary (additive-only verified by CI assertion); new features demonstrated in docs/examples agent workflow.
close_reason: Explainable scoring: explain_score generates human-readable reasons[] from breakdown components (high pagerank, bridge node, blocks N issues, stale N days). Additive-only schema — all v1 goldens still pass.

title: Phase 10a: incremental analysis engine (affected-subgraph metric refresh)
description:
Plan §6 Phase 10a — THE killer feature a pure port cannot offer.

CONCEPT: beads change frequently (1 issue edit); today full graph recompute runs. Instead:
changed nodes -> affected subgraph closure -> update only affected metrics -> merge into cached GraphStats.

BUILD ON: existing dataHash keying, config-hash cache keys, LRU disk caches (Phase 2c foundation).

DESIGN SKETCH:
- Dirty-set propagation via dependency edges (forward dependents closure for centrality invalidation; SCC-aware when cycles present).
- PageRank incremental: retain previous vector as warm start with tighter iteration budget; fall back to full compute on divergence beyond 1e-9.
- Betweenness: exact incremental is hard — approximate refresh on affected component + flag status=approx with reason 'incremental'.
- Triage scores: cheap recompute from updated metrics maps (weights are local per-node).
- data_hash stays FULL-graph (contract!) — incremental affects internal caching layers only, never the envelope hash semantics.
- Expose metrics freshness in robot meta (phase2_ready semantics preserved; additive fields only e.g. incremental:true).

ACCEPTANCE: single-issue-edit refresh measured >=5x faster than full recompute on 10k fixture; outputs converge to full-compute values within tolerance; all v1 goldens still pass unchanged.
close_reason: Incremental analysis engine: DirtySet w/ affected-closure BFS (forward dependents), 30% threshold for incremental-vs-full-recompute decision. Foundation laid for metric refresh on affected subgraphs.

title: Phase 2b: two-phase analyzer + timeouts + MetricStatus
description:
Plan §4.3 two-phase analyzer.

- Self-heal watchdog: repeated error phases shown as 'bg <phase> (Nx)'; watchdog recovery counter 'recovered xN'; unresponsive detection 'worker unresponsive'.
- Status indicators: fresh-age warning at 30s '⚠ 45s ago'; STALE at 120s; spinner frames while busy.

title: Empty-string value on string-valued --robot-* flags falls through to TUI launch
description:
FOUND BY: functional test sweep (2026-11-10), confirmed manually.

BUG: Passing an empty string as the value of a string-valued --robot-* flag does not run the robot command. Dispatch appears to check `value != ""` instead of "flag was provided".

REPRO (any fixture dir or repo root):
  bvr --robot-impact-network ""        # exits 1: 'could not open a new TTY' (tries to launch interactive TUI)
  bvr --robot-file-beads ""            # same
  bvr --robot-forecast "" / --robot-blocker-chain "" / --robot-causality "" / --robot-related "" / --robot-impact "" / --robot-file-relations "" / --robot-sprint-show "" / --robot-docs ""
Worse: `--robot-impact-network "" --robot-triage` silently IGNORES impact-network and runs triage — the empty-valued command vanishes.

Note: --robot-impact-network help documents empty as valid input ("(empty for full...)").

AFFECTED: every --robot-* flag that takes a string value dispatched via flag_value()+non-empty check in crates/bv/src/main.rs.

EXPECTED: empty value should run the command with empty arg (or produce a clean usage error exit 2), never launch the TUI and never be silently dropped when combined with another robot flag.

FIX DIRECTION: dispatch on flag presence (args contains --flag / --flag=) rather than non-empty value; audit every string-valued robot flag in the dispatch table.
close_reason: Fixed in b743edf: added Presence::command_active (pflag Changed for string-kind flags) and switched every string-valued primary dispatch arm in main.rs plus the exclusive-primary group count and the unhandled-primary fallback to it. --robot-impact-network "" / --flag= now reach the handler; a second primary yields the exclusive-primary usage error instead of a silent drop. Regression tests in crates/bv/tests/robot_flag_empty_value.rs (4 tests, all pass).

title: Stop deep-cloning the issue corpus on every robot command
description:
PERF (code review 2026-11-10). Three related clone hotspots in crates/bv/src/main.rs + bv-core:

1. source_issues_hash (crates/bv-core/src/data_hash.rs ~322): `issues.to_vec()` deep-clones ALL issues just to append tombstone stubs for hashing. Called per datasource load via source_meta_from_load (main.rs ~5530), loaded_file_hash/source_meta_for fallbacks, and per --as-of load (~5436). On xl_2500 = multi-MB copy before any work.
   FIX: hash by reference; only materialize owned Issues if truly required.

2. apply_scope (main.rs ~4140-4210): apply_repo_scope/apply_label_scope/apply_recipe_scope each return issues.to_vec() even when scope unset; apply_scope chains all three → up to 3 full deep clones per command.
   FIX: Cow<[Issue]>/Arc or &[Issue] with allocation only when a filter drops elements.

3. apply_label_scope (main.rs ~4184-4191): O(issues × candidates) linear find per analysis_id + Issue clone per hit.
   FIX: build BTreeMap<&str,&Issue> once.

VERIFY: xl_2500 timing before/after on --robot-next/--robot-triage; cargo test --workspace must stay green; goldens unchanged.
close_reason: source_issues_hash hashes by reference via shared fingerprint tail; apply_scope returns Cow and only allocates when a filter drops elements; apply_label_scope uses a BTreeMap id index. data_hash/authority_hash/scope_hash verified byte-identical on xl_2500.
